newsitem.title: USA: "Conspiracy Theory" uncovers top spot at U.S. box office. [CORRECTED 21:29 GMT]
newsitem.headline: "Conspiracy Theory" uncovers top spot at U.S. box office. [CORRECTED 21:29 GMT]

text.p: In the battle of the Hollywood superstars, Mel Gibson and Julia Roberts emerged victorious over Harrison Ford as their "Conspiracy Theory" narrowly replaced his "Air Force One" at the top of the weekend box office, according to studio estimates released on Sunday.
"Conspiracy Theory" earned about $19.4 million for the Friday-to-Sunday period, while "Air Force One" slipped to second with $18.2 million, after spending the previous two weeks at No. 1.
"Spawn" was third with $9.1 million, followed by "George of the Jungle" with $6.3 million and "Men in Black" with $5.7 million.
"Conspiracy Theory" is a Warner Bros. thriller starring Gibson as a New York cab driver who teams up with government official Roberts as one of his wacky cover-up theories comes true.

The movie seemed to inspire some paranoia among rival studios, which pegged the race between the top two as being considerably closer. One onlooker described Warner Bros.' estimate as "rather ludicrous." Still, no one doubted the rankings, and final figures will be issued on Monday. One studio had the movies at $17.9 million and $17.8 million, respectively, while another had them fighting it out in the $18 million range.

"Air Force One," a presidential hijack thriller released by Columbia Pictures, passed the $100 million mark on Saturday, its 16th day of release, as its total rose to $111 million. The studio said this was the fastest R-rated movie to reach $100 million.

Among the other totals, "Spawn" has earned $37.9 (corrects figure from $9.1) million after two weekends, "George of the Jungle" $75.9 million after four weekends, and "Men in Black" $218 million after six weekends.

Warner Bros. is a unit of Time Warner Inc., whose New Line Cinema unit released "Spawn." Columbia, which also released "Men in Black" is a unit of Sony Corp.. Walt Disney Co. released "George of the Jungle."
